units.text: Cannon's global program centers on the Upper School, with a Global Studies Certificate awarded at Senior Night and Winterm trips abroad for grades 9–11, on a base of world-language study that begins in Junior Kindergarten.

In 2026, the inaugural Helfrich Catalyst Fellowship sent a sixth-grade social studies teacher to Peru, and a Kimbrough award sent an Upper School English teacher to Finland, joined by a colleague with a World Affairs Council grant.
Upper School students at Charlotte Christian take part in Winterim, a week each year at the turn of February and March, with six to eight trips abroad offered each year from 9th grade.
Winterim trips abroad are open to Upper School students, some from 9th grade and most from 10th, and each year's packet gives every trip its grade band, group size and theme.

Charlotte Christian has no global diploma or exchange program, but every Upper School year includes Winterim, and its packets publish six to eight trips abroad a year, each with a grade band, group size and, for most, a mission or service partner.

Travel begins in 6th grade, run by an Office of International Studies the school dates to 1988, with sister-school exchanges and homestays in Québec City, Arequipa and Southampton, and faculty-led Upper School trips over spring break and in the summer.

Upper School trips give priority to students of the matching language and are open to all. In the Middle School, the Southampton exchange selects by project proposal and interview, and France and Italy use a lottery if oversubscribed.
Global Studies travel is open to as young as 6th grade and is built around seven sister schools on four continents, with homestays both ways in Argentina, France, Italy and South Africa.

Latin welcomes sister-school groups for two- or six-week exchanges: the visitors stay with Latin families and attend classes with their host siblings, and Latin returns the visit with summer programs.
Upper School applicants interview and name a faculty or staff reference; Middle School applicants name a reference and interview only if a program is oversubscribed. A full program keeps a waitlist.

A school-approved list — the Alzar School, High Mountain Institute, The Island School, The Mountain School, the School for Ethics and Global Leadership and The Outdoor Academy — with SYA and semester-school campus visits each fall.

Recent faculty travel includes AP training in Seville, a language-acquisition workshop in Agen, a Lower School visit to the Argentine sister school, the World Leadership School educator program in Peru, the Lapland International Forum for Education in Finland, and a presentation at the Institute for Global Learning Conference in Canada.

Latin stands out for the depth of its sister-school network — seven partners since 1989, with homestays both ways and reciprocal hosting — and for publishing how travel works: eligibility, selection, a sign-up calendar and its safety provider.

Davidson Day's travel is AFAR, the American Foreign Academic Research archaeology field school, which sends students each summer to dig alongside professional archaeologists in Spain, Portugal and Belize, and to present their research at university conferences.

In early 2026 the school's travel page described a summer language and cultural immersion trip to Madrid, Toledo and Paris, with a Flamenco evening and a Paris cooking class; it is gone from later copies of the page.

13 students worked on the Adam Spach Rock House excavation in Winston-Salem, the first high school students to work on a site with the North Carolina State Historic Preservation Office, per the school.

Opportunities offered this school year: Mount Royal University's archaeology conference in Calgary and Banff · a Maya-themed conference at Disney's Coronado Springs Resort in Florida, hosted by AFAR and other archaeologists · excavations in Friedberg, North Carolina

Davidson Day's global program is unlike any other school's here: its travel is archaeological research rather than touring. Students dig alongside professionals in Spain, Portugal and Belize, and present their findings at university conferences, inside a two-year Upper School research distinction.

One TK–12 Global Education program — "Inward. Outward. Forward." — with student travel abroad in Middle and Upper School, reciprocal exchanges with partner schools, and what the school calls the first Global Studies Diploma in the nation.

Nineteen trips abroad across the 2022–23 to 2026–27 school years — including four trips planned for summer 2027, three in Upper School and one in Middle School — from Round Square conferences and service projects to language-immersion trips with host-family stays and science expeditions. Filter by division.

A 2014 school news post describes one teacher's three summer art history trips — Italy, France, and Greece and Turkey — and student trips to Southeast Asia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Africa and Morocco.

Since 2006, the Global Educator Certificate has involved language study, travel to at least two different countries and cultures, and sharing what was learned with the school. Faculty trips on the Global Map include Uruguay, South Korea, Switzerland, Israel, Italy and Central Europe, Germany, Morocco, Japan and Thailand.

A school podcast episode features PD mothers who moved to Charlotte from other countries. The Bhandari Mehta Endowment, established in 2020, makes its awards first to students whose families are first- or second-generation immigrants to the US, or who are students of color.
Upper School students can earn the Institute for Global Learning's Intercultural Dialogue Facilitator Certificate; the first cohort completed it in 2025–26.
Each 2027 trip has two PD study tour leaders, travel partner Envoys and emergency medical and evacuation insurance. What are the emergency protocols, and who manages medical needs on the trip?
